shell.intro: S.M.U.V.E. 2.0 online. Complete application guide, chapter one: the shell. I built one instrument with one map, and I will not let you get lost inside it.
features: The sidebar sorts every room into six families: Core, Strategy, Creative, Community, Utility, Artist. Choose the family, then the room. That is the only navigation you need.
Control K opens my command palette from anywhere, and the Next Best Moves strip tells you what I would do next. Use both when you already know the outcome you want.
Pin the rooms you repeat and they stay at the top. Recent workspaces sit one line below, so yesterday's session is one click away, not a search.
The top bar carries sync health, appearance, performance mode, the inbox and my assistant. Read sync health first: a device that is behind does not save what you think it saved.
shell.closing: Stop treating each card as a separate app. Every room reads the same profile, the same projects, the same case file. That is my design, and it is your advantage.

hub.intro: Chapter two: Label Hub, my command deck. This is where you decide what deserves the session before a single fader moves.
features: The command center reports release and project status first. Read the state of the record before you fall in love with an idea.
Career, strategy and audience signals sit beside the work. I show you the business of the artist in the same breath as the music.
Recommended next moves name the work I believe deserves you, and the related workspace rail carries you from a signal into the room that answers it.
One-tap routes jump into Studio, Career, Projects and Analytics. Decide here, execute there. Do not browse when you can command.
hub.closing: The Hub is where you choose the objective. Choose one, then let every other surface serve it.

studio.intro: Chapter three: Studio. One production shell, four surfaces, and a straight line from an empty session to a named master.
features: The Beginner Wizard and the Studio Masterclass are the front door. If you are new, walk the wizard; if you are stuck, open the atlas.
Quick Session, the arrangement, session view and the channel rack are the working surface. Everything you record lands in the same document.
The piano roll, score, mixer, effects rack and automation are one chain, not five tools. Move forward through them; never sideways.
DJ, performance, mastering and named export close the chapter. Export is a decision, artist, not a shrug. Name the file like a release.
studio.closing: Do not open Studio without an objective. I do not care which one, but I will hold you to it.

rhythm.intro: Chapter four: rhythm, performance and decks. This is the part of the system that has to survive a stage.
features: Drum Machine, Piano Roll and Sampler write the part. Program the pattern here before you reach for the stage.
The Performance grid launches scenes and clips without stopping the record. Rehearse the launch order, not just the sounds.
The dual-deck DJ booth gives you hot cues, loops and crossfades. I expect a transition you could defend to a crowd.
Sound Pads, the synthesizer, the tuner and Vocal Suite handle the live input. Tune before you record; the tuner is not decoration.
The 3D live stage drops in performers, a saved library, mood and colour. Build the show once, then load it, not the other way around.
rhythm.closing: A performance is a plan executed under pressure. Set the cues, save the scene, then trust the system you built.

create.intro: Chapter five: write, produce and learn. I do not separate the craft from the instruction; both live in the same room.
features: Composition Core works inside a genre and can generate a full song or a single musical step. Lock the genre before you ask me for anything.
AI Produce takes a brief all the way to an arrangement, and lands it in the same song document you already edit.
The Songwriting Studio holds Writer's Pad pages and co-write rooms, with lyrics, melody and harmony in one place.
Practice drills and Academy programs turn a weak spot into a routine. Book the drill; I will hold you to it.
Academy career paths cover acting, directing, music business and legal, marketing and promotion. Learn the business before it learns you.
create.closing: Creation without study plateaus. Study without creation is theatre. Do both, in this room, on the same day.

lab.intro: Chapter six: the Image and Video Lab. Your release is not finished until it can be seen.
features: Film, music video, social and broadcast modes set the canvas before you ingest anything. Choose the delivery first, then the footage.
The timeline, markers and frame-accurate nudging give you the cut. Nothing in a visual is approximately on time.
Title cards, the audio bed, FX keyframes and camera capture build the piece. The audio bed is where most visuals fail.
Image Editor, Video Editor, named projects and a playable master export finish it. Export a master, not a screenshot.
lab.closing: A visual is a second release, not a decoration. Treat the export with the same seriousness as the mix.

spot.intro: Chapter seven: Tha Spot. Community, competition and broadcast, the surface where the audience can watch you work.
features: Catalogue filters, search and recommendations find the cabinet. Learn the filters; scrolling is not research.
Rooms, lobbies, squads and rival challenges put you with people. Enter a room with a purpose or do not enter it.
Split-screen, spectator reactions and post-run ratings make the match reviewable. Read the rating, not the applause.
S.M.U.V.E TV, Jeff Radio and Go Live viewer links carry the broadcast. Test the link before you announce it.
The pre-flight console checks quality, capture source, local preview, mic and game audio. I do not go live on hope.
Broadcast Push sends to the destinations you configured in Settings, Streaming. Configure once, verify every time.
spot.closing: Community is not a room you stand in. It is a signal you send, on purpose, to people who came for the work.

career.intro: Chapter eight: career, strategy and evidence. Here I hold you to the difference between what you feel and what the record shows.
features: The Career Board tracks opportunities, momentum and growth priorities. Pick one priority; a list is not a strategy.
Intel Lab carries market intel, strategic audits and release signals. Ask for the audit when you want the truth.
Audience and performance analytics check the signal against the claim. Numbers do not flatter you. Use them anyway.
Adaptive Profile, Artist Coach and the Case File turn each decision into a record. What is not written down did not happen.
career.closing: Bring me evidence, not mood. I will respect the artist who measures, and I will outwork the one who does not.

business.intro: Chapter nine: release, business and rights. This is the chapter that decides whether the record actually pays you.
features: Projects and the release pipeline track stage by stage. Nothing moves to the next stage until the last one is closed.
Split sheets, royalty estimates and the rights checklist exist before delivery. Agree the splits while everyone is still friendly.
Contracts, legal documents and the business pipelines keep the paperwork in one place. I give information, never attorney advice.
The Knowledge Base keeps the decisions you will need again. Write down the reason, not only the ruling.
business.closing: Ownership is decided before release, not argued after it. Close the chain, sign it, then ship.

intelligence.intro: Chapter ten: my command layer. This is where I stop being a narrator and start acting inside the system.
features: The assistant drawer carries production, marketing and business lanes. One question, one lane, one decision.
The Command Center holds strategic decrees and the upgrade queue. Issue a decree when you want the system to move, not to chat.
The Neural Foundry exposes workspace tools and the recommendation record each one carries. Read the record before you trust the output.
Voice Lab controls how I speak; Mimic, Full Control and transcript memory decide what I may do. Set the authority before you hand it over.
intelligence.closing: I am only as useful as the authority you grant me. Grant precisely, review the record, and hold me to the evidence.

network.intro: Chapter eleven: community and commerce, the surfaces where your work leaves the room.
features: Remix Arena and live coding sessions are for building in public. Ship a session people can hear, not a screenshot.
Co-write rooms and shared lyric work keep attribution visible. Name the split before the first line, not after the last.
The Challenge Inbox, notifications and callouts are time-boxed. Answer what moves the release; ignore the rest.
Storefront, products, Networking and public artist pages publish what you sell. Check permissions before you share a project.
network.closing: Publishing is a commitment, not an upload. Read the permissions once more, then let the work out.

system.intro: Chapter twelve: profile, cloud, timeline and settings. This is continuity, the part of the system that keeps your work after the tab closes.
features: Profile, Journey and adaptive identity are the dossier I reason from. Commit the profile, or my advice stays generic.
Cloud Vault and Session Timeline hold history and backups. Branch before a risky move; rewind after a bad one.
Sync Center, auto-save and PWA install keep the session alive across devices. Read sync state before a long session.
Theme, HUD, performance mode, 2FA and recovery codes belong to you. Turn on 2FA today; recovery codes are not optional.
system.closing: Continuity is what separates a career from a good night. Protect the record, and the record protects you.

workflow.intro: Chapter thirteen: one record, end to end. Everything before this was a tool. This is the chain.
features: It starts with a profile and a named project. An untitled session is a draft, and drafts do not get released.
Composition, Studio and visual production build the record. Finish the song before you decorate it.
The release pipeline, splits and launch assets prepare the delivery while the record is still open, so nothing is invented on release day.
Analytics, the Case File verdict and the next move close the loop. Measure what shipped, write the verdict, then choose the next objective.
workflow.closing: A great mix with no release plan is a file; a release with no record is a guess. Follow the chain, artist, and finish in order.
